forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Barnsley forecasts £1.5m overspend as £1.6m borrowing underspend offsets £3.1m service pressures
news_drafts.lead:
Barnsley Council is forecasting a £1.5m overspend on its day-to-day budget for 2026/27, according to the first-quarter finance report going to Cabinet on 7 October. Services are forecast to overspend by £3.1m as at the end of June. That is partly offset by a one-off £1.6m underspend on corporate budgets, from lower borrowing costs and extra investment income.

Adult social care accounts for £1.5m of the service overspend, and children's social care and the Place directorate £0.9m each. In children's services, 61 children are in external residential placements, against 50 a year earlier, and 93 are with independent fostering agencies, against 76. The report puts each additional residential placement at more than £0.4m a year. A sufficiency strategy approved in April includes three council-led children's homes, but implementation is delayed. Agency staff spending is forecast at £4.3m, against more than £10.6m last year, which the report says shows the reduction programme "starting to have the desired effect".

The council's medium-term financial strategy, its plan showing the gap between expected spending and income, now puts the gap at about £31m to 2029/30. In February it was £23m to 2028/29. The £31m is before the first-quarter pressures, which would take it to £34m unless offset. The 2026/27 budget already uses £4.2m of strategic reserves, money set aside for the council's priorities. The report says further deterioration would mean using reserves earmarked for other priorities and could require savings beyond the £30m already needed.

Separately, the dedicated schools grant, the government grant that funds schools, is forecast to be £13.4m overspent in 2026/27, mainly on high needs, the funding for children with special educational needs. The report expects the deficit to rise by a further £14.6m in 2027/28. Government has extended the statutory override, a rule keeping such deficits off the main balance sheet, until April 2028, but has not published detail on funding for deficits beyond 2025/26.

Capital spending, on things that last, has £21.2m slipping into later years, mostly sustainable transport schemes. Business rates collection is forecast at 96.69% against a 98% target.

news_drafts.headline: Barnsley Council accepts electronic records gap it cannot afford to fix
news_drafts.lead: Barnsley Council's governance and compliance board has formally agreed to accept a risk in electronic records management, determining that available solutions to fix the problem are too expensive to implement. Staff continue reviewing paper records for disposal, but the electronic records management issue remains unresolved. The board's decision reflects resource constraints the council faces in balancing competing budget demands across its services. Electronic records management has not been prioritised for spending at this time.

findings.headline: All 12 core financial system reviews for 2025-26 are completed.
findings.detail: The report says the core system reviews covered transactional and key control testing across 2024/25 and 2025/26. It records excellent co-operation from the Finance Team.
findings.matters: Completed core system reviews are the assurance an external auditor's financial systems work draws on in the accounts audit.
findings.quote: All of the core financial system reviews are completed.

findings.headline: The Glassworks and Alhambra Service Charges review gave limited assurance, with one high-priority implication.
findings.detail: The report says the properties are managed through established governance and senior officer oversight. It found a lapse in timely processes and insufficient evidence that RICS requirements were met and that charges had been benchmarked.
findings.matters: Service charge income that cannot be evidenced as accurate or benchmarked is a point a finance director would track in other councils' commercial and property income.
findings.figures: 1 high, 1 medium, 1 low implication; 2 closed by target date
findings.quote: there was a lapse in timely processes and lack of evidence to provide assurance that RICS requirements were being met, that charges were accurate and that the charges had been benchmarked.

findings.headline: The Procurement Compliance core financial system review gave a 'Reasonable / Limited' opinion, with two high-priority implications.
findings.detail: The report says the corporate procurement framework is in place and strategic procurement is proactive in monitoring non-compliance. It cites continued non-compliant procurement activity within Directorates. Three implications were closed by their target date.
findings.matters: Procurement compliance in directorates is a recurring point of concern for finance directors and lenders reviewing spend control.
findings.figures: 2 high, 1 medium implications; 3 closed by target date
findings.quote: Continued non-compliant procurement activity within Directorates (limited).

findings.headline: Internal Audit delivered 1,661 of 1,831 BMBC corporate assurance days (91%) in 2025-26, an under delivery of 183 days (8%).
findings.detail: The report links the under delivery to a vacant post for part of the year. Corporate Anti-Fraud delivered 410 of 414 revised days (99%) and contingency days were fully used.
findings.matters: A shortfall in assurance capacity affects how much of the control environment can be tested in any year.
findings.quote: The financial year end position for core assurance days relating to the BMBC 2025-26 plan shows an under delivery of 183 days, or 8%, of the original provision.

findings.headline: Financial Management is the second-largest governance domain for 2025-26 implications, at 32 (22%) of 148.
findings.detail: Performance Management and Data Quality is the largest domain at 35 (24%). Financial Management is followed by Information Governance at 20 (14%).
findings.matters: Finance officers at other councils can compare where their own audit findings cluster against this domain breakdown.
findings.figures: Financial Management 32 (22%) of 148 implications; Performance Management & Data Quality 35 (24%)
